input.prompt: A professional woman seated at her desk in a bright modern office, listening. The camera is locked and stationary: ZERO zoom, push-in, pull-out, pan, tilt, crop, reframing, perspective shift or drift. The framing, camera position, subject scale, desk visibility and background composition at the LAST FRAME must be visually identical to the FIRST FRAME - the desk, mug and notebook stay fully in frame the whole clip. She is NOT speaking: lips closed throughout, no lip, mouth or jaw movement. Her eyes look directly into the camera lens the entire clip - no downward glance, side glance, gaze shift, eye wandering or half-lidded look. Only 1-2 brief blinks; eyes otherwise open and steady. A neutral attentive expression that never changes. Head, hair and facial motion at the minimum natural level - only faint breathing. No head turns, tilts, nodding, leaning or gestures. Hands stay as in the source image, loosely clasped and still on the desk. Preserve her face, hair, wardrobe, lighting, colour, the office and desk objects as shown; do not brighten, lift the shadows or re-grade. Wall logo and mug lettering unchanged.
input.negative_prompt: gaze shift, looking down, looking away, eye wandering, head tilt, expression change, excessive facial motion, camera movement, zoom, push-in, pull-out, pan, tilt, reframing, crop, camera drift, perspective shift, speaking, talking, mouth opening, lip movement, gesturing, hand movement, leaning, cut, transition, face change, lighting change, brightening, re-grading, added text, watermark, distortion, warping, morphing

request.prompt_lesson: The first/last-frame clause naming camera position, subject scale, desk visibility and background composition is what holds Kling's camera. The negative prompt does NOT - take 2 carried every camera term in negative_prompt and still pushed in 1.39x. Keep this clause verbatim and keep it at the FRONT of the prompt. Both fields must also stay inside the proven length envelope: prompt <= 1126 chars, negative_prompt <= 435 chars, or the API rejects the request with 'Input exceeds maximum length' (no task created, nothing charged).

correction.what: Removed the temporal brightness/colour drift only. Nothing else was touched.
correction.why: Kling lifted exposure 2.59% peak / 2.27% mean across the 5 s. Known Kling behaviour on every take; the negative prompt does not prevent it.
correction.method: Per-frame per-channel linear gain returning each frame's RGB channel means to frame 0's. Frame 0 is the reference and carries NO gain. Gain range 0.97273 - 1.00000, all <= 1.0, so the correction only scales down - no highlight clipping is possible.
correction.swing_one_sided: 0 of 121 frames darker than frame 0, so the clamp-to-1.0 method applies cleanly. NOTE: take 2's swing was two-sided (22 frames darker) and the clamp method is NOT sufficient in that case - check this before applying the correction to any future take.
correction.filter_shape: format=gbrp16le, then 121 x colorchannelmixer=rr:gg:bb gated by enable='eq(n,N)', then format=yuv420p

fps_note: Base is 24 fps. LatentSync normalises output to 25 fps regardless of input, so the 16-frame padding must be computed at 25 fps (locked rule 3). Same as Diane's base.

accepted_deviation.row: First-frame and last-frame facial expression do not match
accepted_deviation.status: ACCEPTED - NON-BLOCKING. Ruled on by Luis 2026-08-20.
accepted_deviation.measured: Mouth-region mean abs diff frame 1 vs frame 121 is 17.75/255. The lip-aperture proxy runs 90.1 at frame 1, settles to ~69-70 from frame 57 and holds. Visually a soft closed-lip smile relaxes to a neutral, slightly firmer mouth. Face motion 1.989 meanD / 6.178 maxD against an expected band of 0.5-1.5.
accepted_deviation.what_still_matches: Framing, gaze, head position and subject scale all match between first and last frame. Only the expression drifts.
why_accepted: PRECEDENT: Diane's production base carries the identical characteristic. Her sidecar records the residual as 'a slight smile relaxing to neutral and back, plus up to 11 px of permitted head settling', and it was accepted on the same basis. Accepting it here is consistent, not a new concession.

LatentSync re-renders the mouth region during production. Per Diane's record, 'base mouth expression is largely overwritten. What matters is that no speech is baked in - it is not.' No speech is baked in here: lip aperture never approaches the 30 threshold.

Under pingpong the clip reverses at the last frame, so the drift plays as a slow smile-to-neutral-and-back cycle over 10 s rather than a visible jump. The first-vs-last gap of 5.064 is in line with Diane's accepted 4.51.
The eyes - which LatentSync preserves FRAME FOR FRAME, and which caused the take-1 rejection - are correct in this take.
accepted_deviation.residual_risk: Face motion 1.989 remains modestly above both the 0.5-1.5 target band and Diane's accepted 1.67. Recorded so it is a known, deliberate acceptance rather than an unnoticed drift. Revisit only if Roger objects at review.
